title: The Minute Between Episodes
angle: When every spare minute gets filled with audio, quiet can start to feel like a defect rather than a choice.
paragraphs: At an elevator, on the walk to the corner shop, while waiting for water to boil: a pair of earbuds can turn nearly any pause into listening time. There is always another episode, playlist, or voice ready to accompany the next small stretch of the day.

Audio can be good company. A familiar voice makes a repetitive chore less dull, and music can give a commute its own shape. The curious shift comes when an unfilled minute begins to seem unfinished, as though the day has left a blank space that ought to be occupied.

Quiet is not automatically peaceful, and background sound is not automatically a distraction. A busy street, a kettle, the particular hush of a room—these can be welcome or irritating depending on the moment. The difference may be less about choosing the virtuous option than noticing whether the sound is wanted or simply the default.

A walk can have a soundtrack; it can also have traffic, wind, and a thought that takes a while to form. Not every pause needs to become a lesson in mindfulness. Sometimes it is just a minute with nothing playing, which is a perfectly complete use of one.
